name: Systematic Debugging
description: Step-by-step debugging workflow for reproducing and fixing any bug
author: Your Name
usage_notes:
Most useful for bugs that are hard to reproduce.
Always start with reproduction steps before diving into code.
content:
Systematic Debugging

A rigorous, step-by-step approach to debugging any software issue.

Steps

Reproduce the bug — Get a reliable reproduction case. If you can't reproduce it, you can't fix it.
Narrow the scope — Bisect commits, disable features, find the minimal input that triggers it.
Form a hypothesis — What could cause this behavior? Write it down.
Test the hypothesis — Add logging, use a debugger, run experiments.
Implement the fix — Smallest possible change.
Verify — Confirm the bug is gone and no regressions were introduced.
Add a test — Prevent the bug from coming back.

Common Pitfalls

• Changing multiple things at once
• Assuming the bug is in someone else's code
• Skipping reproduction to "just look at the code"

name: handoff-codex
description: 长会话结束前自动生成交接文档，写入项目 handoff/ 目录，涵盖当前进度、已完成项、阻塞点、下一步和避坑指南。
author: chengxuan
usage_notes: 适合多轮长对话、暂停工作、或用户说"交接/保存进度/记录一下"时使用。脚本路径为 scripts/create_handoff.sh。
content:
Handoff Codex

长会话结束前生成一份交接文档，让下一次会话（或接手的人）能快速接上进度。

何时使用

• 即将结束一轮多轮对话，手头还有进行中的工作
• 用户明确说 handoff / 交接 / 保存进度 / 记录一下
• 暂停复杂工作，稍后再继续
• 任务做到一个自然的停顿点

工作流程

确定项目根目录 —— 通常是当前工作目录。不确定就问用户。
运行脚本创建文件：
   
   脚本会创建 handoff/ 目录和 handoff-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.md 文件，并输出文件路径。
打开生成的文件，用当前对话的具体信息填充每个章节。
向用户确认已创建的文件和位置。

写作指南

具体、事实。每个章节都要有可操作的信息，而不是模糊的总结。

现在做什么

• 当前正在进行的具体任务或目标
• 哪些文件正打开 / 正在编辑
• 当前采用的方法或策略
• 接手的人马上需要知道的上下文

已经完成了什么

• 已完成的工作项，带文件路径，不要感受
• 关键决策及其原因
• 提交、分支、或产出的文件
• 跑过的测试及其结果

卡在哪里

• 确切的阻塞点或待解决问题
• 试过但不奏效的方法
• 不确定或未知的地方
• 缺少什么信息

下一步做什么

• 有序的下一步行动列表
• 优先级很重要
• 每一项要具体到让一个刚接手的人知道该做什么

哪些坑不要再踩

• 已经探索过的具体错误或死路
• 环境配置的陷阱
• 看起来能行但实际不行的事
• 任何不明显的行为或配置

注意事项

• 默认用中文写；如果对话是英文的就切英文
• 简洁但完整：优先用要点和具体细节，不用大段散文
• 有帮助的地方加上文件路径和行号
• 不要跳过任何章节 —— 如果某节是空的，写"无"或"暂无"并简要说明原因
• 写多了比写少了好

name: Code Review Assistant
description: Structured code review checklist and feedback format
author: Example Author
usage_notes: Good for PR reviews. Customize the severity rubric to match your team's standards.
content:
Code Review Assistant

Helps conduct thorough, consistent code reviews.

Review Dimensions

• Correctness: Does the code do what it intends to?
• Security: Any vulnerabilities or injection risks?
• Performance: Unnecessary work? O(n²) where it should be O(n)?
• Readability: Clear naming, consistent style, good comments?
• Tests: Are there tests? Do they cover the important cases?

Feedback Format

Start with severity:
• 🔴 Blocking — must fix before merge
• 🟡 Warning — should fix, discuss if unsure
• 💡 Suggestion — optional improvement
• ❓ Question — need clarification

name: Refactoring Workflow
description: Safe, incremental refactoring approach that doesn't break things
author: Marketplace Author
usage_notes:
The "test first" rule is the most important one.
Don't refactor code that doesn't have tests — write tests first.
content:
Refactoring Workflow

Safe refactoring in 6 steps.

Steps

Ensure tests exist — If no tests, write them first. You need a safety net.
Run tests, confirm they pass — Green baseline.
Make a small refactoring — One change, one concept.
Run tests again — Should still pass.
Commit — Small, atomic commit.
Repeat — Next small refactoring.

Rules

• Never refactor and add features in the same commit
• If tests fail after a refactoring, revert — don't debug forward
• Rename before you restructure
